name: Badger
tagline: Pure-Go LSM key-value store that separates keys from values to cut write amplification.
description: Badger is an embeddable, persistent key-value store written in pure Go, created by Dgraph Labs as the storage engine for the Dgraph graph database. It follows the WiscKey design: keys live in the LSM tree while larger values go to a value log, which keeps the tree small and reduces write amplification on SSDs. It offers serializable snapshot-isolation transactions, TTLs, encryption at rest and a change subscription API, without cgo. Ownership passed from Dgraph Labs to Hypermode and, in October 2025, to Istari Digital with the rest of Dgraph; releases have continued in the v4 line. Value-log garbage collection needs attention in write-heavy deployments.

scale.notes: Single-process library; terabyte-scale stores are used under Dgraph.

strengths: Pure Go with no cgo, so builds and cross-compiles cleanly
Key-value separation reduces write amplification for larger values
Built-in TTL, encryption at rest and an in-memory mode
Subscribe API streams key changes to the application
weaknesses: Value-log garbage collection must be scheduled and tuned
Ownership changed twice since 2023 (Hypermode, then Istari Digital)
Higher memory use than B-tree stores like bbolt
useCases: Storage layer for Go databases and services
Embedded state for Go daemons and CLIs
Write-heavy local key-value workloads with medium-to-large values
notIdealFor: Distributed storage without an extra layer
